Hi Olga / Marissa / Ben,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We're kicking off the technical side of the onboarding and want to lock down a few items so our engineers can finish the network and identity changes on their side. High-level asks:

- Confirm SAML assertion lifespan and recommended NameID format for Okta.
- SCIM: we need the full attribute map and an example PATCH flow for group assignments.
- IP allowlist: we'll supply office and peering ranges but want to confirm whether Redwood supports CIDR ranges for both hosted and dedicated.
- Service accounts: we need guidance on least-privilege scopes for token exchange and rotation cadence.

I've attached our SAML metadata (saml_metadata.xml) and a short SCIM schema doc to illustrate our current directory layout. Can you confirm what's required from Redwood and whether any org policies (e.g., MFA enforcement, session expiry) will need to be pre-configured before cutover?

Subject: Re: Fintegrity: initial SSO/SCIM/allowlist details and constraints

Hi Alice — great to get these. Quick answers inline, and I've attached our SCIM attribute mapping template for your team to fill.

- SAML assertion lifetime: Redwood recommends <= 5 minutes for SPA flows, 10 minutes for server-side flows. We can accept up to 15 minutes if your IdP restricts short TTLs, but for tight session gating we recommend 5–10m.
- NameID format: we prefer persistent NameID urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:nameid-format:persistent or emailAddress for compatibility with downstream auditing.
- SCIM: attached is the scim-attribute-mapping-template.xlsx. Please populate the externalId, userName, givenName, familyName, email, active, and groups columns. We'll implement PATCH semantics for group add/remove; see our example in the template.
- IP allowlist: Redwood supports CIDR ranges for both hosted and dedicated. For hosted, allowlist is evaluated at edge; for Dedicated, we can apply per-cluster network ACLs.
- Service accounts: create two service accounts for the integration — one for provisioning (SCIM_write) and one for runtime token exchange (inference_token). We recommend rotating keys every 90 days; if you need automated rotation we can propose a script + API.

Org policies: MFA enforcement and SSO-only for admin roles should be applied prior to go-live. Session duration and consent prompts can be configured on our side but we require the admin role and service accounts to be whitelisted in your IdP.

Next steps:
1) Fintegrity to return the populated SCIM mapping template (requested by Mar 6).
2) Redwood to share a preflight checklist and a proposed test cutover window (I can do Mar 14 or Mar 15).
3) Joint tech call to validate SAML metadata and run a test assertion.

I've uploaded the template and a short preflight checklist to the shared doc: https://redwood.app/docs/onboarding/fintegrity-map-7521

Best,
Olga Petrov
Principal, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

1) Assertion lifetime: Okta currently issues 30m by default. We can make a per-application override to 10m for Redwood. Will proceed if you confirm 10m is supported.
2) NameID: we plan to use persistent.
3) SCIM PATCH: we included an example where we update group membership via PATCH; confirm Redwood honors 'schemas' and supports path=Operations in the PATCH body.
4) Service account rotation: Fintegrity prefers an automated rotation cadence. Do you have a recommended script or can Redwood rotate via API?

Alice — all noted and looks good. Quick confirmations and scheduling: 

- 10m assertion lifetime: confirmed, Redwood supports 10-minute assertions for application sessions. We'll mirror your IdP per-application override.
- SCIM PATCH: we support RFC7644 PATCH semantics and honor 'schemas' arrays in the request. Our implementation uses externalId as the canonical key by default; we'll accept userName if externalId is empty but prefer externalId.
- Service account rotation: Redwood exposes a rotation endpoint in the APIs (POST /v1/service-accounts/{id}/rotate) and we can share a small script that calls it and stores the new key in your Vault. I'll drop the script into the shared Drive link after the tech call.
- CIDR allowlist: confirmed for both hosted and dedicated; for dedicated we'll also provide a per-cluster ACL snippet and Helm values examples.

Tech call: I'm available Mon Mar 13 at 09:00 PT or Tue Mar 14 at 11:00 PT. Please confirm which works for Fintegrity and we'll send an invite that includes the runbook PR and preflight checklist.

Final preflight checklist (summary):
- SCIM mapping populated and delivered — received.
- SAML metadata validated against our parser — validated.
- IP ranges submitted — waiting on txt (received in Alice's forwarded attachment).
- Service accounts provisioned and key rotation plan agreed — action item to provision.

If we get the tech call scheduled for Mar 13/14 we should be able to run the test assertion and a one-way SCIM group add/remove test, then decide go/no-go on Mar 16. I'll prepare the runbook PR and post the link here once it's ready.

Thanks — looking forward to the cutover.
